note: Ranked tiers the assistant supports, and how each maps onto the public MLBB statistics API. The API exposes rank buckets all|epic|legend|mythic|honor|glory — there is no separate Mythical Immortal bucket, so Immortal reads Glory data and the UI says so rather than pretending the numbers are its own.

tiers.label: Epic
tiers.blurb: Solo-carry environment. Draft for heroes that win their lane without help.

tiers.label: Legend
tiers.blurb: Objectives are contested but rarely set up. Tempo still beats composition.

tiers.label: Mythic
tiers.blurb: Rotations appear. Counters start to matter as much as raw hero strength.

tiers.label: Mythical Honor
tiers.blurb: Drafts get answered. Flex picks and lane-swap threats gain value.

tiers.label: Mythical Glory
tiers.blurb: Near-tournament habits. Composition and CC chains decide fights.

tiers.label: Mythical Immortal
tiers.fallbackNote: The public data source has no Immortal bucket — showing Mythical Glory statistics.
tiers.blurb: Every draft is scouted. Comfort matters less than the matchup you are handing over.

rankCurve.note: meta adjustment = skillWeight x (difficulty - 3) x factor. A mastery hero gains priority as the rank climbs; a pick-up-and-play hero loses it. Only applied when live rank statistics are unavailable — real pick/ban/win rates always win.
